title: Functional Decomposition and Shapley Interactions for Interpreting Survival Models
claim: Real-world data with feature interactions is decomposed by a functional framework, then interaction effects are interpreted over time.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, arrows between stages, mini plots per function
description: A three-stage left-to-right figure with bold titles over each stage. Left: 'Model Real World Survival Data with Interactions' shows a blood-test/AIDS ribbon icon and a CD4 cell icon linked by circular black arrows, labeled Prior AIDS diagnosis and CD4 Cell Count. Middle: 'SurvFD: Rigorous framework to discern interactions' shows axes with three curves (log hazard in blue, hazard in orange, survival in purple) labeled 'Obtain survival prediction functions'. Colored arrows lead to three small stacked plots (log hazard, hazard, survival) showing decomposed time-dependent effects, labeled 'fANOVA feature effects'. Right: 'SurvSHAP-IQ: Interpret interaction effects' shows a time-series plot of many noisy lines for cd4 × priorzdv, colored by high/low combinations (red, orange, green, blue) with a legend. Black arrows join the stages.
caption: SurvFD and SurvSHAP-IQ facilitate the interpretation of interactions in survival models. (images: Flaticon.com)
abstract: Hazard and survival functions are natural, interpretable targets in time-to-event prediction, but their inherent non-additivity fundamentally limits standard additive explanation methods. We introduce Survival Functional Decomposition (SurvFD), a principled approach for analyzing feature interactions in machine learning survival models. By decomposing higher-order effects into time-dependent and time-independent components, SurvFD offers a previously unrecognized perspective on survival explanations, explicitly characterizing when and why additive explanations fail. Building on this theoretical decomposition, we propose SurvSHAP-IQ, which extends Shapley interactions to time-indexed functions, providing a practical estimator for higher-order, time-dependent interactions. Together, SurvFD and SurvSHAP-IQ establish an interaction- and time-aware interpretability approach for survival modeling, with broad applicability across time-to-event prediction tasks.
